_comment: FA -- flattened audio. Every person in the group gets their own audio part and
their own photograph, each preceded by a text part naming them, and the person
of interest is named only in user_prompt_template, at the very end.
The turn this produces, for a group of participants 1, 3 and 4:
text   preamble
text   audio_label(1)   audio  <participant 1's track>
text   audio_label(3)   audio  <participant 3's track>
text   audio_label(4)   audio  <participant 4's track>
text   image_label(1)   image  <participant_1.png>
text   image_label(3)   image  <participant_3.png>
text   image_label(4)   image  <participant_4.png>
text   video_label      video  <sampled frames>
text   system_prompt + user_prompt_template
PEOPLE ARE LISTED IN ASCENDING ID ORDER, never participant-first. Withholding
the person of interest until the end only means anything if the ordering does
not leak it. modes/fa.py sorts; do not reorder here.
LABELS ARE WHAT BINDS AN ID TO A TRACK. They are real text parts sitting
immediately before each media part, so the association does not depend on
part order the way PA's inert '<audio1>' markers do. {speaker_id} is the
only placeholder they take. Rewording them is fine; dropping the id is not.
user_prompt_template is rendered against the record's fields plus, from
modes/fa.py render_user_prompt:
{participant}  the person of interest
{goa_ids}      every id in the group, comma-separated, ascending
{other_ids}    the group minus the person of interest
{goa_size}     how many people are in the group
({conversation_floor} does NOT render: the flattener keeps only scalars, and
it is a list.)
system_prompt: You are a helpful multimodal assistant.
preamble: You will be shown, for each person in a conversation group, their own audio recording and a photograph of them, each labelled with their participant number. After that you will see a video of the group.
user_prompt_template:
You have now seen all {goa_size} people in this group: participants {goa_ids}. Each audio recording is that one person's own voice, and each photograph shows that one person.

Identify the intentions of participant {participant} during this clip.

An intention is what the participant appears to want to achieve, based on what they seem to believe is happening and what they seem to want. Focus on intentions, not just visible actions.

Use observable visual and audio cues, the overall tone of the interaction, the situation type, and likely social scripts to support your interpretation. You can tell who participant {participant} is from their photograph and their voice, and you can use the other participants ({other_ids}) to understand what they are responding to. Give your best intuition even when the intention is subtle or ambiguous.

For each intention you identify, answer in this format:

1. Timestamps: [start time] [end time]
2. Intention: [brief description of what the participant is trying to do or achieve]
3. Confidence in interpretation: [1-5]
4. Why: [observable cues plus your interpretation of the participant's beliefs/desires and the situation]
5. Confidence in explanation: [1-5]
6. Intensity: [1-5 rating of how strong or high-priority the intention appears]
7. Counterfactual explanation: [an alternative interpretation that would change the understood intention]

If the full clip contains no clear intention, answer only:

No clear intention: yes
Why: [brief explanation]
